lesson.title: Same centre, different spread

steps.headline: The range is the largest value minus the smallest. It measures spread.

lead.text: The gap you just found has a name: the range. It is one way to measure spread, how far apart the values lie. Both buses have the same mean, yet their gaps differ.
The first list is 4, 4, 4, 4. The second is 2, 2, 6, 6. Work out each mean, then picture where the points sit.

reveal.text: Both have mean 4. The four 4s sit on one spot. The 2s and 6s lie two either side. Same centre, different spread.

steps.headline: The standard deviation is the typical distance from the mean.

lead.text: To use every value, measure each distance from the mean and square it. The average of those squares is the variance. Its square root is the standard deviation, in the data's own units.
Each list here is a whole population, so divide by the count. A sample usually divides by one less.

steps.headline: Find the population variance of 1, 1, 1 and 9.

workedSteps.text: Find the mean: the total over the count.
Square each distance from the mean.
These are 4, 4, 4 and 36. Add them and divide by four.

steps.headline: Find the population standard deviation of 2, 2, 6 and 6.

workedSteps.text: The mean is 4. Every value is 2 away, so every squared distance is 2 × 2.
Divide by how many values there are.

lead.text: Same steps, new numbers. The mean is still 4, but the values sit further out.

reveal.text: You found each distance, squared it and averaged. A wider list gives a larger variance with the same mean.

lead.text: Back to Bus B, late 0, 0, 20 and 20 minutes. Treat the four days as the whole population. Bus A, always 10 minutes late, has a standard deviation of zero.

reveal.text: The standard deviation is in minutes, the same units as the data. Two buses with the same mean are told apart.

lesson.orientation: Compare datasets with the same mean, and distinguish range from population variance and standard deviation.
lesson.nextAction: Try a new case and return for recall after a delay.

blocks.text: Two buses both average 10 minutes late. Look at how differently they get there.

intro.promise: By the end you'll tell two lists with the same mean apart, using the range and the standard deviation.

recap.keyIdea: The range uses only the largest and smallest values. The variance and standard deviation use every value's distance from the mean, so lists with the same mean can differ in spread.

blocks.text: You compared 4, 4, 4, 4 with 2, 2, 6, 6. Both have mean 4. For 2, 2, 6, 6 the range is 4 and the standard deviation is 2.

recap.nextHook: You rarely measure a whole population. What can a sample tell you about it?

questions.prompt: What is the range of 2, 2, 6 and 6?
hints: Subtract the minimum from the maximum.
Repeated values do not change which endpoints are smallest and largest.
Subtract the smallest endpoint, 2, from the largest endpoint, 6.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The largest value is 6 and the smallest is 2; the range is 6 − 2 = 4.

questions.onCorrect: 4. The range is the largest minus the smallest, so the repeats make no difference.

misconceptions.feedback: That adds the two extremes. Compare them another way.
That is the largest value. Compare it with the smallest.

questions.prompt: What is the population standard deviation of 2, 2, 6 and 6?
hints: What is the mean? How far is each value from it?
Every value is the same distance from the mean. Square that distance.
The squares average to the variance. Take its square root.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: All four squared distances from the mean 4 are 4. Variance is 16/4 = 4; its square root is 2.

questions.onCorrect: 2. Every value is 2 from the mean, so the squares average to 4 and the root is 2.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the variance. The standard deviation is its square root.
That is the sum of the squared distances divided by two. Use the count of values.

questions.prompt: What is the population variance of 0, 0, 8 and 8?
hints: Square each distance from the mean of 4.
The mean is 4; compute the squared distance of each 0 and each 8.
Add those four squared distances and divide by the whole-population count of four.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Each squared distance from mean 4 is 16. Their average is 64/4 = 16.

questions.onCorrect: 16. Each value is 4 from the mean, and 4 × 4 is the squared distance.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the standard deviation. Variance is the average of the squared distances, before the root.
That is the total of the squares. Divide by how many values there are.

questions.prompt: What is the range of 3, 4, 4, 7 and 13?
hints: Only the two endpoints determine the range.
The interior values do not affect a range calculation.
Use only the maximum 13 and the minimum 3.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The maximum minus the minimum is 13 − 3 = 10.

questions.onCorrect: 10. Only the largest and smallest count: 13 − 3. The middle values play no part.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the largest value. The range compares it with the smallest.
That adds the extremes. The range is their difference.

questions.prompt: Bus A is exactly 10 minutes late on each of four days. Bus B is late by 0, 0, 20 and 20 minutes. Both average 10 minutes. What is the gap between Bus B's best day and its worst day, in minutes?
hints: Which day was Bus B's best, the least late?
Its worst day is the most late. How many minutes is that?
Take the smaller from the larger.
questions.onCorrect: 20 minutes. Bus A has no gap at all, though both buses average the same.

misconceptions.feedback: That is Bus B's average. The question compares its two extreme days.
That is the total lateness over four days. Compare only the best and worst days.

questions.prompt: The lists 4, 4, 4, 4 and 2, 2, 6, 6 are compared. What is the relationship?
hints: Work out each mean. Then look at where the points sit.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Both lists average 4. The first has no deviation from it, while the second lies two below or above.

questions.onCorrect: Same mean of 4, different spread. A centre on its own cannot tell these lists apart.

misconceptions.feedback: Work out each mean first: do the lists really differ there?
Same average does not mean the points sit in the same places. Compare where they lie.

questions.prompt: A list is a whole population, and a second list is a sample from a larger group. What differs in the variance?
hints: Is every member of the group in the list, or only some?

acceptedIdeas: A whole-population variance divides by its count; the usual sample estimate divides by one less
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: For the full population, divide the squared distances by their count. The usual estimate from a sample divides by one less, because the mean was itself estimated.

choices.label: A whole-population variance divides by its count; the usual sample estimate divides by one less
Population variance divides only by the largest value

questions.onCorrect: A whole population divides by its count. A sample usually divides by one less.

misconceptions.feedback: Averaging means dividing by something. Ask what the squared distances are divided by.
The largest value has nothing to do with how many values there are.

questions.prompt: Why square each distance from the mean?
hints: Add the distances 1 − 3, 1 − 3, 1 − 3 and 9 − 3. What do you notice?

acceptedIdeas: Distances below the mean would cancel distances above it
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Distances below the mean are negative and above are positive, so they cancel. Squares are never negative.

choices.label: Distances below the mean would cancel distances above it
The mean is always a square

questions.onCorrect: Distances below the mean cancel distances above. Squares are never negative, so they all count.

misconceptions.feedback: Squaring a number above 1 makes it bigger. Think about the signs of the distances.
The mean can be any number. Think about what happens to negative distances.

questions.prompt: Each squared distance is 4. What is the total of the four squared distances?
hints: Four equal numbers are added.
Four lots of the same number: use multiplication.
Multiply the squared distance by how many values there are.
questions.onCorrect: 16. Add the squared distances; the next move is to average them.

misconceptions.feedback: That is one squared distance. Add all four.

questions.prompt: Average the four squared distances. What is the population variance?
hints: Divide the total by how many values there are.
Four values, so divide by four.
Take the total of the squares and share it over the four values.
questions.onCorrect: 4. Variance is the average squared distance from the mean.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the total of the squares. Divide by how many values there are.
Dividing by one less is for samples. This list is the whole population.

questions.prompt: Bus B is late 0, 0, 20 and 20 minutes, a whole population. What is its population standard deviation, in minutes?
hints: Find the mean first. How far is each day from it?
Square that distance, then average the squares.
The average of the squares is the variance. Take its square root.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Each day is 10 from the mean, squares 100, variance 100, standard deviation 10.

questions.onCorrect: 10 minutes. Bus A has none at all: that is the difference the mean hides.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the variance. Take its square root to return to minutes.
That is the range. Use every day's distance from the mean instead.

questions.prompt: What is the population standard deviation of 3, 3, 9 and 9?
hints: Find the mean first.
Every value is the same distance from the mean. Square that distance.
The squares average to the variance. Its square root is the standard deviation.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The mean is 6, every value is 3 away, variance 9, standard deviation 3.

questions.onCorrect: 3. The mean is 6 and every value is 3 away, so the root of the average square is 3.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the variance. The standard deviation is its square root.
That is the mean. Spread is about distance from it.

questions.prompt: The squared distances from the mean of a whole population are 2, 4 and 6. What is the variance?
hints: The variance is the average of the squared distances.
Add the squared distances, then divide by how many there are.
Divide the total of the squares by three.
questions.onCorrect: The variance is the average squared distance from the mean.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the total of the squares. Divide by how many values there are.
That divides by two. Use the count of values.
